detail.longDescription: # Uber Data Breach Exposes Thousands of Drivers’ Personal Information Through Third-Party AI Provider Uber has confirmed a data breach involving personal information belonging to thousands of U.S. drivers after attackers compromised credentials at Fireworks AI, a third-party technology provider. Here are the key findings: * Attack Vector: Attackers compromised internal credentials at Fireworks AI and used them to gain unauthorized access to Uber data stored with the provider. * Exposed Information: Stolen records included drivers’ license information and other personal details. * Scope of Impact: At least 7,870 individuals across Massachusetts, South Carolina, and Rhode Island have been identified in breach notifications. The total number of affected individuals remains unknown. * Discovery and Response: Uber was notified on October 9, 2026, and confirmed unauthorized access four days later. The company subsequently disconnected its data connections with the provider. * Additional Exposure: The same Fireworks AI incident also affected Notion, demonstrating how a single third-party compromise can have consequences across multiple organizations. * Mitigation: Uber says it has not identified evidence of misuse and is offering affected individuals free credit monitoring and fraud assistance. My Takeaway: This incident is another reminder that an organization’s security perimeter extends well beyond its own infrastructure. Third-party vendors, AI platforms, APIs, and external service providers can all become entry points into sensitive corporate data. As organizations increasingly integrate AI services into their applications and workflows, vendor security assessments, credential management, least-privilege access, and continuous monitoring need to be treated as essential security controls, not afterthoughts. Your security is only as strong as the ecosystem you depend on. # CyberSecurity # DataBreach # ThirdPartyRisk # SupplyChainSecurity # ArtificialIntelligence # CloudSecurity # InfoSec Source: https:// cybersecuritynews.com/uber-con firms-data-breach/
